issueTitle: Agents in the Wild: Security Holes, Benchmark Lies, and One Actual Shipping Thing
editorLetter:
The theme this week is trust—and how little of it is warranted.

On the security side: tool specifications in AI agents are a bigger attack surface than most teams realize. Schema-formatted tool definitions change model behavior in ways that degrade safety, and KV cache reuse opens a new class of injection vectors. These aren't theoretical. If you're shipping agentic systems, this cluster deserves a read before your next deploy.

On the measurement side: a validity audit of four major agent-safety benchmarks found their scores are being quoted interchangeably as if they measure the same thing. They don't. R-Judge, InjecAgent, AgentHarm, AgentDojo—all measuring different behaviors, all getting cited as 'safety.' The EvalSafetyGap survey reinforces this: benchmark scores can improve while actual alignment properties stay flat or get worse.

The one genuinely useful shipping item: Google's Gemini 3.6 Flash with managed agents and lifecycle hooks. Not revolutionary, but it's production infrastructure you can use today.

Everywhere else, the pattern is researchers identifying real problems—LLMs failing in clinical reasoning, code agents avoiding deletion, long-context models copying instead of reasoning—and offering partial fixes. Good signal, but none of it is plug-and-play.

The EU AI content labeling mandate went live. Start your compliance checklist now if you haven't.

sections.title: The 5 That Matter
sections.description: Stories with direct production implications this week

stories.title: Gemini 3.6 Flash Ships with Managed Agents and Lifecycle Hooks
stories.label: Tool
stories.blurb: Google expanded the Gemini API's Managed Agents offering with the 3.6 Flash model, lifecycle hooks, and infrastructure aimed at production-grade reliability. This is the most concrete agent platform update from a major cloud provider this week—not a paper, an actual API.
stories.whyItMatters: Managed agent infrastructure from Google means less glue code for developers and a clearer path to production. Hooks enable pre/post-action control, which matters for safety and observability.
stories.takeaway: If you're building on Gemini, evaluate the managed agent layer before rolling your own orchestration.

stories.title: Tool Schemas Are an Underestimated Attack Surface in AI Agents
stories.label: Signal
stories.blurb: Schema-formatted tool definitions—the JSON specs that tell agents what tools exist and how to call them—measurably degrade safety behavior in LLMs. The paper identifies this as a primary, poorly-understood source of safety regression when deploying agents with external tools.
stories.whyItMatters: Every agentic system uses tool specs. If the format itself is influencing unsafe behavior, this is a systemic issue, not a model-specific one.
stories.takeaway: Audit your tool schemas. Minimal, precise specs may be safer than richly-documented ones.

stories.title: Agent-Safety Benchmark Scores Are Not Interchangeable—Validity Audit Shows Why
stories.label: Research
stories.blurb: Researchers ran R-Judge, InjecAgent, AgentHarm, and AgentDojo across 22 models under official implementations. The benchmarks measure different behaviors but their scores get cited as equivalent proxies for 'agent safety.' They aren't. Correlation between benchmarks is weak.
stories.whyItMatters: If you're selecting models or vendors based on safety benchmark scores, you may be comparing apples to motorcycles. This paper is a prerequisite for any procurement or red-teaming process.
stories.takeaway: Require benchmark-specific breakdowns, not aggregate safety scores, when evaluating agent systems.

stories.title: EU AI-Generated Content Labeling Is Now Mandatory
stories.label: Policy
stories.blurb: The EU's requirement for companies to label AI-generated content is now in force. This applies broadly to companies deploying generative AI systems that produce content visible to EU users.
stories.whyItMatters: Non-compliance is a legal risk, not just a reputational one. If your product generates text, images, or video for EU audiences, you need a disclosure mechanism.
stories.takeaway: Audit your user-facing AI outputs now. Build labeling into your content pipeline, not as an afterthought.

stories.title: LLMs Pass Medical Exams But Fail Real Clinical Reasoning
stories.label: Signal
stories.blurb: A clinical perspective paper argues that despite exam-passing performance, LLMs lack the reasoning patterns required for safe autonomous clinical decision support. The gap between benchmark performance and real-world clinical reasoning remains wide and dangerous.
stories.whyItMatters: Medical AI is being deployed faster than the evidence supports. This is a calibration check for anyone building or procuring clinical decision tools.
stories.takeaway: Don't conflate benchmark performance with clinical readiness. Human oversight is non-negotiable for now.

sections.title: Builder Notes
sections.description: Practical research and tools for teams shipping agent systems

stories.title: ARCTIC: AI Code Review That Prioritizes Correctness Over Style
stories.label: Tool
stories.blurb: ARCTIC is a code critique system designed for AI-generated diffs at scale. Unlike existing tools that over-index on style, it targets correctness, security, and performance—the things human reviewers actually care about. Addresses the review bottleneck as coding agents generate more volume than teams can handle.
stories.whyItMatters: Code review is the chokepoint in AI-assisted development. A tool that filters noise and surfaces real issues is immediately useful.
stories.takeaway: Evaluate ARCTIC against your current AI code review setup, especially if you're running coding agents in CI.

stories.title: LLMs Avoid Deleting Code—Here's How to Measure and Fix It
stories.label: Research
stories.blurb: LLMs editing code have a systematic bias toward addition over deletion, even when deletion is the correct action. The paper quantifies this 'deletion avoidance' and proposes mitigation strategies. Real problem for anyone using LLMs for refactoring or dead code removal.
stories.whyItMatters: If your coding agent is making codebases larger instead of cleaner, this explains why and offers a path forward.
stories.takeaway: Explicitly prompt for deletion when refactoring. Measure add/delete ratios in agent-generated PRs.

stories.title: SREGym: A Live Benchmark for Testing AI Agents on Real Infrastructure Failures
stories.label: Tool
stories.blurb: SREGym provides high-fidelity, extensible failure scenarios for benchmarking AI SRE agents against production-like conditions. Previous SRE benchmarks were too simplistic and hard to extend. This one exposes a live environment API for realistic testing.
stories.whyItMatters: If you're building or evaluating agents for incident response, you need a benchmark that reflects real failure modes, not toy scenarios.
stories.takeaway: Use SREGym to stress-test agent incident response before giving it production access.

stories.title: HijackKV: KV Cache Reuse Opens a New Injection Vector
stories.label: Signal
stories.blurb: Position-independent KV cache reuse—used to speed up inference—creates a new attack surface where cached context from one session can be exploited in another. HijackKV demonstrates this threat class and its implications for multi-tenant agent deployments.
stories.whyItMatters: KV cache sharing is common in production inference stacks. If you're running shared infrastructure, this is a live security concern.
stories.takeaway: Review your inference stack's cache isolation policies, especially in multi-tenant or multi-user deployments.

stories.title: CodeRescue: Budget-Aware Error Recovery Routing for Coding Agents
stories.label: Research
stories.blurb: CodeRescue routes failed coding agent attempts to stronger models based on budget and failure type, rather than simple cascade escalation. In executable environments, failure produces actionable feedback—this system uses that feedback to route smarter.
stories.whyItMatters: Cost-aware agent routing is a real engineering problem. Smarter recovery beats naive 'try again with GPT-4' escalation.
stories.takeaway: Model your agent failure modes explicitly. Budget-calibrated routing beats static escalation policies.

sections.title: Research Worth Skimming
sections.description: Papers with real signal, but not yet production-ready

stories.title: Benchmark Scores Can Improve While Actual Safety Stays Flat—A 373-Paper Survey
stories.label: Research
stories.blurb: EvalSafetyGap synthesizes 373 papers to document the measurement gap between LLM evaluation metrics and actual safety properties. Benchmark scores, reward signals, and safety metrics can all trend upward while underlying alignment properties remain uncertain or unchanged.
stories.whyItMatters: Foundational critique of how the field measures progress. Relevant for anyone making deployment decisions based on published safety numbers.
stories.takeaway: Treat published safety scores as necessary but not sufficient. Require behavioral red-teaming alongside benchmarks.

stories.title: VLMs Hallucinate When Commonsense Priors Override Visual Evidence
stories.label: Research
stories.blurb: Vision-language models systematically override clear visual evidence with commonsense priors—reporting five fingers on a visibly six-fingered hand, for example. The paper shows these errors are directional and proposes selective prior calibration to mitigate them.
stories.whyItMatters: Multimodal agents relying on VLMs for perception can fail in predictable, systematic ways. Understanding the failure mode is the first step to guarding against it.
stories.takeaway: Test your VLM pipeline with atypical visual inputs. Don't assume visual evidence dominates model priors.

stories.title: DynaResize: Runtime GPU Reallocation Cuts Pipeline Bubbles in RL Post-Training
stories.label: Research
stories.blurb: RL-based post-training disaggregates rollout and training across separate GPU pools, but static partitioning creates severe pipeline bubbles under long-tail latency. DynaResize dynamically reallocates GPUs between stages to balance execution and reduce waste.
stories.whyItMatters: If you're running RL post-training at scale, static GPU allocation is likely leaving significant throughput on the table.
stories.takeaway: Worth benchmarking against your current RL training infrastructure if you're doing RLHF or GRPO at scale.

sections.title: Noise Check
sections.description: Things getting attention that don't warrant it

stories.title: AIvilization: Large-Scale AI Social Simulation Is a Research Demo, Not Infrastructure
stories.label: Ignore
stories.blurb: AIvilization v0 simulates large-scale artificial societies with LLM agents under resource constraints. Interesting as a research artifact for studying emergent multi-agent behavior. Not useful for production systems. The 'publicly deployed' framing overstates practical relevance.
stories.whyItMatters: Multi-agent simulation research has a long road to production applicability. File under 'watch in 3 years.'
stories.takeaway: Skip unless you're doing academic multi-agent systems research.

stories.title: Nightcrawler: Local Pentesting Agent on a Smartphone
stories.label: Tool
stories.blurb: Nightcrawler is a fully local AI pentesting agent running on smartphones. Early-stage (12 HN points, 4 comments). Concept is interesting—edge-deployed security tooling without cloud dependency—but maturity is unclear. Worth bookmarking, not deploying.
stories.whyItMatters: Edge-deployed security agents are a real direction. This specific implementation needs more validation before trust.
stories.takeaway: Monitor the repo. Don't use in any real engagement yet.

oneThingToTry: Run your current agent's tool specifications through a minimal-spec rewrite: strip descriptions to only what's necessary for correct invocation, remove examples, and tighten enum constraints. Then re-run your existing safety evals. The Tool Specifications paper suggests schema verbosity correlates with safety degradation—this is a zero-cost experiment you can run this week.
watchNext: How inference stack vendors respond to HijackKV: KV cache isolation will become a selling point or a liability depending on who moves first.
Whether the EU AI content labeling mandate triggers similar moves in the UK, Canada, or US states—the compliance surface is about to get larger.
ARCTIC (AI code critique) in practice: does prioritizing correctness over style actually change PR merge rates or defect escape rates at scale?
Clinical AI regulation: the gap between LLM exam performance and clinical reasoning is documented—watch for FDA or EMA guidance tightening deployment criteria.
Agent memory systems maturing: ECHO, AttriMem, and MemForest all shipped this week. Convergence on a standard memory interface for long-horizon agents would be a significant unlock.
